images.caption: Figure 1:Motivation and overview of ReFocus.(a)Sparse terminal rewards reveal little about partial progress or task-specific bottlenecks.(b)ReFocus uses progress feedback to guide targeted practice through alternation of Global RL and Local RL.(c)ReFocus achieves success rates of 98.3% on three real-world long-horizon tasks, compared with 81.7% for RECAP[1].(d)ReFocus raises the success rates ofπ0.5\pi_{0.5}[5]from 90.6% to 97.8% on LIBERO-Long and from 39.3% to 51.3% on RoboCasa365.

Figure 2:Illustration of ReFocus.(a)Global RL uses task DAGs to assign progress rewards and track subtask completion.(b)The Scheduler selects Adaptive Practice Windows for bottleneck practice. Three rollout modes connect local practice with full-task execution, while milestone rewards provide finer feedback.(c)Multi-round training alternates Global and Local RL. Full-task feedback and practice costs are recorded in the history buffer to guide subsequent practice.

Figure 3:Qualitative results on RoboCasa365.Rows (a)–(d) show rollouts from the SFT policy and policies after Alternating Optimization rounds 1–3, respectively. Red boxes highlight failures. T denotes the first successful environment step.
Figure 4:Credit assignment with Progress Reward.With fixed critic predictions, Progress Reward increases the GAE advantages of completed subtasks and milestones in a failed rollout.

Figure 6:Qualitative comparison on real-world tasks.RECAP misses a grasp inPickFruit(top) and gets stuck inBreadBaker(bottom). ReFocus-based adaptation completes both tasks. Smaller images show wrist-camera views. Red boxes mark failures.
Figure 7:Real-world task setups.We conduct three long-horizon tasks, with circled numbers indicating the order of execution.
Figure 10:Visual input for the Scheduler during bottleneck diagnosis.Each cell shows synchronized left, right, and wrist-camera views, together with the control step and task stage.
Figure 11:Representative RoboCasa365 scenes for training, validation, and testing.
Figure 13:Real-world task execution sequences.Rows (a)–(c) showPickFruit,StackBowl, andBreadBaker, respectively.

Figure 14:Value predictions on real-robotBreadBakerrollouts.Critics trained with and without progress rewards are evaluated on a successful episode (left) and a failed episode (right). Green and red dots mark progress and failure-related events.
